questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the autobiography 'Lone Fox Dancing: My Autobiography'?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ruskin Bond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ruskin Bond** is a renowned Indian author of British descent known for his extensive contributions to English literature in India.
 
• His autobiography, **'Lone Fox Dancing'**, provides a detailed account of his life, including his childhood, career, personal experiences, and insights into his literary journey.
 
• The book captures his **solitary yet enriching life**, his love for nature, and his deep connection with India, particularly the Himalayan region.
 
• **Ruskin Bond** has authored numerous novels, short stories, and essays, many of which reflect his affinity for simple village life, nature, and relationships.
 
• He was honored with the **Padma Shri** in 1999 and the **Padma Bhushan** in 2014 for his immense contribution to literature.
 
• Some of his notable works include **'The Room on the Roof,' 'A Flight of Pigeons,'** and **'The Blue Umbrella.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khushwant Singh**__

 __
 
• **Khushwant Singh** was a famous Indian author, lawyer, diplomat, journalist, and politician.
 
• He is best known for his novel **'Train to Pakistan'**, which depicts the partition of India in 1947.
 
• He was known for his wit and humor, as well as his bold and candid opinions on various societal and political issues.
 
 
 
• **Brij Mohan Kaul**__
 __
 
• **Brij Mohan Kaul** was a distinguished Indian Army officer and strategist.
 
• He played a significant role in the Indian military operations during the early years after independence.
 
• However, he is not related to the field of literature or the writing of autobiographies.
 
 
 
• **John Dalvi**__
 
 
• **John Dalvi** was an Indian Army officer and the author of the book **'The Himalayan Blunder.'**
 
• His work is a critical account of India's military failure during the 1962 Sino-Indian War.
 
• He is not associated with the autobiography **'Lone Fox Dancing.'**

questions.question: In which of the following years did the battle of Plassey take place?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1757**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Plassey** was fought on **23rd June 1757**.
 
• It was a significant event in Indian history as it marked the beginning of **British political control in India.**
 
• The battle was fought between the forces of **Siraj-ud-Daulah**, the Nawab of Bengal, and the **British East India Company**, led by **Robert Clive.**
 
• The British achieved victory due to the betrayal by **Mir Jafar**, one of Siraj-ud-Daulah's commanders, who sided with the British.
 
• The victory in this battle allowed the British East India Company to establish a stronghold in **Bengal**, which later expanded to other parts of India.
 
• This victory also enabled the Company to collect **revenue** from the province of Bengal, strengthening their financial and military position.
 
• The Battle of Plassey is often considered the starting point of **British colonial dominance** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Important Points about the Battle of Plassey:**__

 __
 
• The term **Plassey** comes from the village **Palashi**, located near the battlefield, on the banks of the **Bhagirathi River** in present-day West Bengal.
 
• The battle is a classic example of **divide-and-rule tactics** employed by the British to gain political and territorial control.
 
• **Robert Clive** was instrumental in strategizing and ensuring the British victory.
 
• Post-battle, Mir Jafar was installed as the **puppet Nawab of Bengal** by the British.
 
• The victory at Plassey laid the foundation for the **Battle of Buxar (1764)**, which further solidified British dominance in India.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Battle:**__
 
 
• It marked the **beginning of British colonial rule** in India.
 
• The British East India Company gained significant territorial and economic advantages.
 
• The battle showcased the importance of **strategy** and **alliances** in warfare.

questions.question: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma is associated with which of the following dances?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a **classical dance form** originating from the state of **Andhra Pradesh, India**.
 
• It derives its name from the village **Kuchipudi** in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma is a renowned **Kuchipudi exponent** and has made significant contributions to this art form.
 
• This dance combines **grace, fluid movements, and narrative storytelling**, often depicting themes from Indian mythology.
 
• Kuchipudi performances include both **solo and group acts**, with emphasis on expressions (abhinaya) and intricate footwork.
 
• It is performed with a mix of **dancing, acting, and music**, making it unique among Indian classical dances.
 
• The traditional attire for Kuchipudi dancers includes rich costumes and **ornate jewelry**, which highlight the elegance of the dance.
 
• Some famous Kuchipudi compositions are based on **epics like Ramayana and Mahabharata**, as well as devotional themes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Odissi**__

 __
 
• **Odissi** is a classical dance form from **Odisha, India**.
 
• It is characterized by its **soft, lyrical movements** and strong devotional themes, often dedicated to Lord **Jagannath**.
 
• Odissi is predominantly performed by women, with intricate hand gestures and poses.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**__
 __
 
• **Kathakali** originates from **Kerala, India** and is known for its elaborate costumes, makeup, and masks.
 
• This dance-drama focuses on **mythological stories** and involves intense facial expressions and gestures.
 
• Kathakali performers undergo rigorous training to master the art of communicating emotions through facial expressions and body movements.
 
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam**__
 
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is another classical dance form from **Kerala, India**.
 
• This dance is characterized by its **graceful, feminine movements** and is often referred to as the dance of the **"Enchantress."**
 
• Mohiniyattam performances typically convey themes of **love and devotion**.

questions.question: Sanchi stupa was rediscovered in the year _______ by General Henry Taylor.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1818**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sanchi Stupa** is one of the oldest stone structures in India and is a significant Buddhist monument.
 
• It was originally commissioned by **Emperor Ashoka** in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• The stupa is located in **Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh**, India.
 
• It is renowned for its **architectural grandeur** and its importance in Buddhist history.
 
• The rediscovery of the Sanchi Stupa in **1818** is credited to **General Henry Taylor**, a British officer.
 
• Before its rediscovery, the site had been abandoned for centuries and was in a state of disrepair.
 
• The rediscovery marked a significant milestone in the study of India's ancient history and Buddhist art.
 
• After its rediscovery, the stupa underwent **restoration and conservation efforts** during the British era.
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is part of a larger complex that includes **other stupas, monasteries, and temples**, showcasing Buddhist art and architecture.
 
• The stupa is adorned with intricately carved gateways called **toranas**, depicting scenes from the life of Buddha and Jataka tales.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Importance of Sanchi Stupa**__

 
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is a UNESCO **World Heritage Site**, recognized for its cultural and historical significance.
 
• The monument is a classic example of **Mauryan architecture** and Buddhist art.
 
• Sanchi serves as a major tourist destination and an important site for scholars studying **Buddhism and ancient Indian history**.
 
• The site emphasizes Emperor Ashoka's contribution to spreading **Buddhism** across India and beyond.

questions.question: In November 2023, who was appointed as the Chief Information Commissioner of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Heeralal Samariya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Heeralal Samariya** was appointed as the **Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) of India** in **November 2023**.
 
• The **Chief Information Commissioner** is responsible for ensuring the implementation of the **Right to Information (RTI) Act**, which aims to promote transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities.
 
• **Heeralal Samariya** is a retired **Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer**, known for his extensive experience in governance and administration.
 
• His appointment was made in accordance with the provisions of the **Right to Information Act, 2005**, which mandates the selection of the CIC through a committee comprising the **Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition, and a Union Cabinet Minister.**
 
• As CIC, **Heeralal Samariya** will play a pivotal role in addressing grievances related to the denial of information and ensuring that the citizens' right to information is upheld.
 
• The tenure of the CIC is **five years** or until the age of **65 years**, whichever is earlier.
 
• The office of the CIC is of significant importance in empowering citizens to seek information from public authorities and ensuring **good governance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Randeep Guleria**__

 __
 
• **Randeep Guleria** is a renowned **pulmonologist** and the former director of the **All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi**.
 
• He has been instrumental in India’s fight against the **COVID-19 pandemic**, offering expert advice on public health measures.
 
 
 
• **Rajiv Gauba**__
 __
 
• **Rajiv Gauba **served as the **Cabinet Secretary of India** from** 2019 to 2024**, holding the position for the longest tenure with four extensions, and as of March 2025, he is a **full-time member of NITI Aayog.**
 
 
 
• **Arvind Subramanian**__
 
 
• **Arvind Subramanian** is an eminent **economist** and served as the **Chief Economic Adviser (CEA) of India** from 2014 to 2018.
 
• He is widely known for his contributions to economic policies and his work on the **Economic Survey of India**.

questions.question: Stunted growth, which is common in children growing up in extreme poverty, is a sure sign of __________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Undernutrition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Stunted growth** refers to impaired growth and development that children experience due to **chronic undernutrition**, particularly during the first 1,000 days of life.
 
• **Undernutrition** is the primary cause of stunting and is typically a result of a combination of inadequate nutrient intake and recurrent infections.
 
• Children suffering from stunting are often shorter than their peers and may have **lower cognitive and physical development levels**.
 
• Stunted growth is closely associated with **extreme poverty**, where access to sufficient and nutritious food is severely limited.
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** emphasizes that stunting is a critical indicator of child health and nutrition, affecting approximately **22% of children under five years globally** as per recent statistics.
 
• It is often an indicator of long-term **economic and social disadvantage** and can perpetuate the cycle of poverty.
 
• Efforts to reduce stunting include addressing **maternal nutrition**, promoting exclusive breastfeeding, ensuring access to **nutrient-rich foods**, and improving sanitation and healthcare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lack of Clothing**__

 __
 
• While a lack of clothing is often associated with extreme poverty, it does not directly cause stunted growth.
 
• Clothing primarily serves the purpose of **protection against environmental conditions**, but it is not linked to the physiological development of children.
 
 
 
• **Sleep Deprivation**__
 __
 
• Sleep is important for **overall growth and development**, but sleep deprivation alone is not a primary factor for stunted growth.
 
• It may contribute to other health issues, such as cognitive impairments, but is not a leading cause of stunting.
 
 
 
• **Lack of Housing**__
 
 
• Lack of housing is a major challenge for families living in poverty but does not directly cause stunted growth.
 
• However, poor housing conditions can lead to **exposure to infections and diseases**, which might contribute indirectly to undernutrition.

questions.question: In which of the following cities was the headquarters of Theosophical Society established in British India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Adyar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Theosophical Society** was established in **1875** in New York by **Madame Blavatsky** and **Colonel Olcott**. It aimed to promote universal brotherhood, study ancient religions and philosophies, and explore the mysteries of nature and humanity.
 
• Its headquarters were moved to **Adyar**, a locality in **Chennai (then Madras), Tamil Nadu**, in **1882**. This location became a global hub for the society’s activities and teachings.
 
• The Adyar campus is situated on the banks of the **Adyar River**, covering a vast area of lush greenery, and it includes a library, gardens, and meditation spaces.
 
• The Theosophical Society at Adyar played a significant role in influencing Indian spiritual leaders, philosophers, and reformers like **Dr. Annie Besant**, who later became its president and contributed to India’s freedom movement.
 
• The society's teachings emphasized the study of **comparative religion, philosophy, and science**, fostering the idea of unity among all religions and cultures.
 
• Adyar remains an important center for those interested in theosophy, spirituality, and interfaith dialogue.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ayanavaram**__

 __
 
• **Ayanavaram** is a locality in **Chennai, Tamil Nadu**. It is known for its residential and commercial mix but does not have any historical or spiritual connection to the **Theosophical Society**.
 
 
 
• **Ashok Nagar**__
 __
 
• **Ashok Nagar** is another area in **Chennai**, primarily recognized as a residential and commercial neighborhood. It has no association with the activities or history of the **Theosophical Society**.
 
 
 
• **Alandur**__
 
 
• **Alandur** is a locality in the suburbs of **Chennai**, known for its metro station and residential zones. It holds no relevance to the establishment or functions of the **Theosophical Society**.

questions.question: If the server manages to land a legal serve and the receiver is unable to return the ball, it is known as an ace and the server gets the point. Which of the following sport is referred here?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tennis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **ace** in tennis refers to a **legal serve** that the receiver fails to touch or return, resulting in the server winning the point outright.
 
• Aces are considered a mark of **skill and precision** in tennis, as they require the server to deliver a fast and accurate serve that is difficult to return.
 
• The serve must land in the **service box** on the opponent's side of the court to be considered legal.
 
• The **speed** and **placement** of the serve play a significant role in achieving an ace.
 
• Famous tennis players like **Roger Federer, Serena Williams, and Novak Djokovic** are known for their ability to serve aces consistently.
 
• In professional tennis, aces are often used as a **strategy to dominate service games** and reduce the opponent's chances of breaking serve.
 
• Scoring in tennis follows a unique system (15, 30, 40, game), and an ace directly contributes to advancing the score in favor of the server.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wrestling**__

 __
 
• **Wrestling** is a combat sport that involves grappling techniques such as throws, takedowns, joint locks, and pins.
 
• It is one of the **oldest forms of combat sports**, dating back to ancient civilizations like Greece and Rome.
 
• Modern wrestling includes styles like **freestyle, Greco-Roman, and professional wrestling.**
 
• Unlike tennis, wrestling does not involve serves or aces but focuses on physical strength and technique.
 
 
 
• **Boxing**__
 __
 
• **Boxing** is a combat sport in which two participants throw punches at each other with gloved hands.
 
• It is governed by rules that determine the duration of rounds, scoring, and permissible techniques.
 
• Boxing terms include **knockout (KO), technical knockout (TKO), and unanimous decision,** which differ significantly from tennis terminology.
 
 
 
• **Shooting**__
 
 
• **Shooting** is a sport that involves testing accuracy and precision using firearms or air guns.
 
• It is an Olympic sport with events such as **10m air rifle, 25m pistol, and trap shooting.**
 
• The concept of scoring in shooting is based on hitting targets, which differs entirely from the scoring system in tennis.

questions.question: At which of the following places is the Lalbagh Flower Show organised, where thousands of flower varieties are put on display in different forms with a particular theme (which changes every year) during the exhibition?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bengaluru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lalbagh Flower Show** is one of the most famous exhibitions in **Bengaluru**, Karnataka.
 
• It is held at the **Lalbagh Botanical Garden**, which is known for its rich collection of tropical plants and historical significance.
 
• The show is organized **twice a year**, during **Republic Day (January) and Independence Day (August)**.
 
• The event attracts thousands of visitors, showcasing a variety of **flowers, plants, and artistic flower arrangements.**
 
• Each year, the flower show is based on a particular **theme** reflecting important cultural, historical, or environmental topics.
 
• The **Lalbagh Botanical Garden** was commissioned by **Hyder Ali** in the 18th century and later expanded by his son **Tipu Sultan.**
 
• The flower show includes artistic recreations of monuments, scenes, and sculptures made entirely from flowers.
 
• The event is managed by the **Department of Horticulture** and is considered a significant cultural attraction in Bengaluru.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Patna**__

 __
 
• **Patna**, the capital city of Bihar, is famous for its historical sites such as the **Golghar, Patna Sahib Gurudwara, and Kumhrar archaeological sites.**
 
• It is not known for organizing any significant flower shows like Bengaluru's Lalbagh Flower Show.
 
 
 
• **Hyderabad**__
 __
 
• **Hyderabad** is renowned for its historic monuments such as the **Charminar** and **Golconda Fort**, as well as the **Ramoji Film City.**
 
• It hosts various cultural events but does not hold a flower show comparable to the Lalbagh Flower Show in Bengaluru.
 
 
 
• **Patiala**__
 
 
• **Patiala**, a city in Punjab, is known for its rich cultural heritage, including the **Patiala Peg** and the **Qila Mubarak complex.**
 
• It does not organize any significant flower exhibitions like Bengaluru.

questions.question: According to Census of India 2011, which is the largest religious community in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hindus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census of India 2011**, Hindus form the largest religious community in India.
 
• The **Hindu population** constitutes approximately **79.8%** of the total population of India, making it the majority religion in the country.
 
• **Hinduism** is one of the oldest religions in the world and is often referred to as a **way of life**.
 
• The religion is characterized by a diversity of beliefs and practices, including the worship of a vast number of deities such as **Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Durga, and Lakshmi**.
 
• Important texts in Hinduism include the **Vedas, Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, and Ramayana**.
 
• Major Hindu festivals celebrated in India include **Diwali, Holi, Navratri, Dussehra, and Makar Sankranti**.
 
• India is home to several prominent Hindu pilgrimage sites, such as **Varanasi, Rishikesh, Haridwar, Tirupati, and Puri**.
 
• The majority of the Hindu population is concentrated in states such as **Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal, and Tamil Nadu**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Christians**__

 __
 
• **Christianity** is the third largest religious community in India, constituting approximately **2.3%** of the total population as per the **Census of India 2011**.
 
• Christianity was introduced to India by **St. Thomas, one of the apostles of Jesus Christ**, around 52 CE.
 
• Major Christian communities are concentrated in states like **Kerala, Goa, Nagaland, and Mizoram**.
 
• Important Christian festivals include **Christmas, Easter, and Good Friday**.
 
 
 
• **Muslims**__
 __
 
• **Islam** is the second largest religion in India, with approximately **14.2%** of the population identifying as Muslims as per the **Census of India 2011**.
 
• India has the **third-largest Muslim population in the world**, after Indonesia and Pakistan.
 
• Muslims in India are predominantly concentrated in states like **Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Kerala**.
 
• Important Islamic festivals celebrated in India include **Eid-ul-Fitr, Eid-ul-Adha, and Muharram**.
 
 
 
• **Sikhs**__
 
 
• **Sikhism** is a monotheistic religion founded in the **15th century** by **Guru Nanak** in the Punjab region.
 
• Sikhs constitute approximately **1.7%** of the total population of India as per the **Census of India 2011**.
 
• The majority of Sikhs in India reside in the state of **Punjab**.
 
• The **Golden Temple** in Amritsar is one of the most important pilgrimage sites for Sikhs.
 
• Key Sikh festivals include **Guru Nanak Jayanti, Baisakhi, and Guru Gobind Singh Jayanti**.

questions.question: The Narora _______ Power Station is located in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Atomic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Narora Atomic Power Station** is located in the state of **Uttar Pradesh**, India.
 
• It is a part of India's **nuclear power program** and is operated by the **Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL).**
 
• The power station has two operational units with a capacity of **220 MW each,** using **Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs).**
 
• It was commissioned in the year **1991** and plays a significant role in meeting the energy demands of northern India.
 
• The facility uses **uranium** as fuel, and heavy water acts as both a **moderator and coolant** in the reactors.
 
• Nuclear power plants like Narora are known for their ability to produce large amounts of electricity with minimal **greenhouse gas emissions.**
 
• It adheres to strict safety protocols and is under the supervision of India's **Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Natural Gas**__

 __
 
• **Natural gas** power plants use a **clean-burning fossil fuel** to generate electricity.
 
• They are widely used for **peak load electricity generation** and in areas where gas supplies are abundant.
 
• Unlike nuclear power, natural gas plants emit **carbon dioxide (CO₂),** a greenhouse gas, during operation.
 
• India's major natural gas-based power plants include the **RGPPL (Ratnagiri Gas and Power Pvt. Ltd.)** and the **Dadri Gas Power Plant.**
 
 
 
• **Wind**__
 __
 
• **Wind power** plants convert the kinetic energy of wind into electricity using **turbines.**
 
• It is a form of **renewable energy** and does not produce greenhouse gases.
 
• India's leading wind power-producing states include **Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.**
 
• One of the largest wind farms in India is the **Muppandal Wind Farm** in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: To which of the following classes of compounds does cyclohexane belong?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Alicyclic compound**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclohexane** is classified as an **alicyclic compound** because it is a cyclic compound that contains only single bonds and does not exhibit aromaticity.
 
• An **alicyclic compound** is a compound that has both **aliphatic** and **cyclic characteristics**, meaning it is non-aromatic.
 
• **Cyclohexane's structure** is composed of six carbon atoms arranged in a closed ring, with each carbon atom bonded to two hydrogen atoms.
 
• Unlike aromatic compounds, **cyclohexane** does not contain delocalized π-electrons or a conjugated ring structure.
 
• The chemical formula of cyclohexane is **C₆H₁₂**, and it is commonly used as a **non-polar solvent** in laboratories.
 
• Cyclohexane is known for adopting a **chair conformation** to minimize strain and achieve stability.
 
• Examples of other alicyclic compounds include **cyclobutane** and **cyclopentane**, which also lack aromaticity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Non-benzenoid aromatic compound**__

 __
 
• A **non-benzenoid aromatic compound** is one that exhibits **aromaticity** but does not contain a benzene ring.
 
• Such compounds follow **Hückel's rule** (4n+2 π-electrons) but have a different cyclic structure, such as **tropolone** or **cyclopropenyl cation**.
 
 
 
• **Heterocyclic compound**__
 __
 
• A **heterocyclic compound** is a cyclic compound that contains at least one atom other than carbon in the ring, such as **nitrogen, oxygen, or sulfur**.
 
• Examples of heterocyclic compounds include **pyridine**, **furan**, and **thiophene**.
 
 
 
• **Benzenoid aromatic compound**__
 
 
• A **benzenoid aromatic compound** contains a benzene ring or a similar structure with delocalized π-electrons.
 
• Examples include **benzene**, **toluene**, and **naphthalene**.

• The **Women’s Reservation Bill 2023**, officially known as **The Constitution (One Hundred Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023**, was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **Tuesday, September 19, 2023.**
 
• This bill seeks to reserve **33% of seats in the Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assemblies** for women.
 
• The bill aims to increase the **representation of women** in India's legislative bodies, addressing a longstanding demand for **gender parity in politics.**
 
• The introduction of the bill coincided with the **special session of Parliament** held in September 2023, marking a historic moment in Indian politics.
 
• Once enacted, the bill will amend the **Constitution of India**, specifically Articles relating to the composition of legislative bodies, to include provisions for the reservation of seats for women.
 
• The bill's implementation is expected to take place after the completion of the next Census and the subsequent delimitation exercise, as stated by the government.
 
• This step is being lauded as a significant move toward achieving **gender equality** in political representation.

• 126th Constitutional amendment Bill:

• This amendment also removes the provision of nominating two Anglo - Indian communities in Lok sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following Parts of the Indian Constitution mentions about the relations between the Union and the States?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Part XI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XI** of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the **Relations between the Union and the States**.
 
• This part includes **Articles 245 to 263**, which outline the legislative, administrative, and financial relations between the Union and the States.
 
• It is divided into two chapters: **Chapter I - Legislative Relations** and **Chapter II - Administrative Relations**.
 
• Article 245 defines the **extent of laws** made by Parliament and the Legislatures of States.
 
• Articles 246 to 254 deal with the **distribution of legislative powers** between the Union and the States, based on the Union, State, and Concurrent Lists.
 
• Articles 256 to 263 focus on administrative relations, including the **obligations of States and the Union** and the coordination between them.
 
• These provisions ensure the **division of powers** and responsibilities, maintaining the federal structure of governance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Part VIII**__

 __
 
• **Part VIII** of the Indian Constitution deals with the **Union Territories**.
 
• It includes **Articles 239 to 241**, which provide the framework for the **administration of Union Territories**.
 
• Union Territories are directly governed by the **Central Government**, although some have legislative assemblies, like Delhi and Puducherry.
 
 
 
• **Part X**__
 __
 
• **Part X** focuses on the administration of **Scheduled and Tribal Areas**.
 
• It includes **Articles 244 and 244A**, which provide special provisions for the governance and protection of the rights of **Scheduled Tribes**.
 
 
 
• **Part VII**__
 
 
• **Part VII** initially dealt with provisions related to **Part-B states**, which were later removed after the reorganization of states in India.
 
• It became **redundant** after the Seventh Amendment to the Constitution in **1956**.

questions.question: Where of the following was Bal Gangadhar Tilak's Home Rule Movement active?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__.

__
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** was one of the leading figures in the Indian Independence Movement and is regarded as the "Father of Indian Unrest."
 
• Tilak's **Home Rule Movement** was primarily active in the state of **Maharashtra**, where he had a strong base of followers.
 
• The movement, started in **1916**, aimed at achieving self-governance for India and inspired people to actively participate in the freedom struggle.
 
• The Home Rule Movement in Maharashtra focused on **creating awareness** about self-rule and the need for independence from British colonial rule.
 
• Tilak used his newspapers, **Kesari** (in Marathi) and **Mahratta** (in English), to mobilize public opinion and spread the message of the movement.
 
• The movement emphasized the importance of **Swadeshi goods** and self-reliance, encouraging people to boycott British-made goods.
 
• Tilak's leadership in Maharashtra was complemented by **Annie Besant's efforts** in other parts of India, such as Madras.
 
• The movement also laid the foundation for future mass movements, including Mahatma Gandhi's **Non-Cooperation Movement.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bihar**__

 __
 
• Bihar was not a major center of Tilak's Home Rule Movement, but it played a significant role in other parts of the freedom struggle, especially under leaders like **Rajendra Prasad** and **Jayaprakash Narayan.**
 
 
 
• **Madras**__
 __
 
• The Home Rule Movement in Madras was spearheaded by **Annie Besant**, who worked tirelessly to promote self-rule in southern India.
 
• She established the **Home Rule League** in Madras in 1916 and mobilized people through her speeches, writings, and organizational efforts.
 
 
 
• **Punjab**__
 
 
• While Punjab was a significant region in India's freedom struggle, it was not the main focus of Tilak's Home Rule Movement.
 
• Punjab saw the rise of freedom fighters like **Lala Lajpat Rai** and later played a major role in movements like the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre protests.**

• He was a significant ruler in the **Mauryan dynasty**, which played a crucial role in Indian history during the ancient period.
 
• Bindusara's reign marked the continued consolidation of the vast Mauryan Empire established by his father.
 
• He was known as **Amitraghata**, meaning "Slayer of Enemies" in Sanskrit.
 
• His administration maintained the policies and governance established by **Chandragupta Maurya** and his advisor **Chanakya**.
 
• Bindusara ensured stability and unity in the empire, which laid the foundation for his son **Ashoka** to rise to prominence later.

 __

• Chandragupta's mentor and advisor **Chanakya** (Kautilya) was instrumental in shaping the empire's policies and governance.

• He embraced **Buddhism** after the Kalinga War and promoted non-violence and dharma throughout his reign.
 
• Ashoka's reign is noted for the spread of Buddhism and his inscriptions, including the famous **Edicts of Ashoka**.

• The article reflects the guiding principles of India's **foreign policy** and is inspired by the **ideals of the United Nations Charter.**
 
• The inclusion of Article 51 showcases India’s commitment to being a responsible member of the global community and advocating for **peaceful coexistence**.
 
• It also highlights the importance of fostering respect for international law and treaty obligations.
 
• Although the DPSPs are **non-justiciable**, they act as guiding principles for the government while framing policies and laws.

 __
